title: EOSC Node | Italy - Home
main_text: Italy's national node of the European Open Science Cloud Candidate EOSC Node · build-up phase Italy EOSC Node | Italy Federating Italian research data, high-performance computing, cloud infrastructure and digital services for FAIR, secure and cross-disciplinary science in Europe. Sign in with EOSC AAI Explore the Node Catalogue Explore Node resources This Node Landing Page is publicly accessible without login. Protected resources must present an EOSC-AAI access route and their User Access Policy before the user enters. Scope and users Resources Policies Governance Helpdesk EOSC Node | Italy Official Tripartite-approved name · Coordinated and operated by ICSC View the dedicated Node page on eosc.eu → Node scope Federated computing, data and digital services for European research EOSC Node | Italy connects national research infrastructures, service providers, e-infrastructures and repositories to the EOSC Federation. The Node integrates high-performance computing, cloud, storage, data analysis, catalogues, authentication and training capabilities. Its objective is to enable cross-Node workflows, FAIR research outputs, secure analysis of sensitive data, and the responsible adoption of artificial-intelligence and quantum technologies. Its scientific scope includes HPC, cloud and quantum computing, astrophysics, life sciences, physics, environmental research and AI/ML applications. Intended users Researchers in Italian and European universities and research organisations National and European research infrastructures and e-infrastructures Data stewards, repository managers and FAIR-enabling teams Research software engineers and workflow developers Communities using HPC, cloud, AI and quantum capabilities Educators, trainers, students and research-support professionals Node capabilities From discovery to federated analysis 1 Discover Find national research products, Open Access publications, datasets, software and services through interoperable catalogues. 2 Compute Use federated HPC and cloud centres, certified cloud regions and emerging quantum-computing pilots. 3 Analyse Run Jupyter notebooks, interactive environments and reproducible REANA workflows close to the data. 4 Collaborate Work through VREs, training environments and integrated file synchronisation and sharing. 5 Federate Combine identity, registries, catalogues, workflows, compute and storage across organisations and Nodes. 6 Reuse Apply metadata registries, semantic-interoperability policies and FAIR practices to research outputs. Responsible organisation ICSC — Italian Research Center on High Performance Computing, Big Data and Quantum Computing ICSC coordinates and operates the Node, federating resources from more than 50 participating organisations. Access principle Public information, federated access Public pages and catalogues are anonymous. Protected services use EOSC-compliant federated authentication and must state whether access is open, moderated or restricted. Node Exchange resources Discover resources and understand their conditions Every production resource offered through the Node must provide an English purpose description, Acceptable Use Policy and User Access Policy both along this public discovery journey and in its Node and EOSC Catalogue metadata. Node Catalogue Public discovery Discover the services, datasets, software, workflows and other research products currently offered by EOSC Node | Italy. UAP: Catalogue records must be publicly readable. Contribution or curation functions may require EOSC AAI and an assigned role. AUP: The infrastructure policy and any provider-specific conditions linked by the individual record. Browse the Node Catalogue Infrastructure AUP/UAP Data repositories and research products Record-specific Discover and reuse Open Access publications, datasets and other research artefacts exposed by national repositories. UAP: Public records and open resources are anonymous; protected content must provide an EOSC-AAI access route or clearly state its provider authorisation process. AUP: The licence, attribution requirements and provider conditions displayed in each catalogue record. Find repository resources Research artefact policy HPC, cloud and storage EOSC AAI + allocation Provide federated computing and storage through national HPC centres, cloud providers and ISO 27001-certified cloud regions. UAP: Authenticate through EOSC AAI. Eligibility, approval, quotas, allocation periods and provider requirements must be stated in the selected resource record. AUP: Provider AUP, security rules, fair-use limits and applicable infrastructure conditions. Find compute resources EOSC AAI sign-in Reproducible workflows EOSC AAI Execute containerised analytical workflows, including REANA pipelines, across federated resources and close to large datasets. UAP: Authenticate through EOSC AAI; workflow execution, resource sizes and allocations follow the conditions of the selected service. AUP: Service and provider AUPs, software licences, data conditions and resource-consumption limits. Find workflow services EOSC AAI sign-in Interactive environments and VREs EOSC AAI Use Jupyter notebooks, interactive analysis environments, Virtual Research Environments and collaborative research tools. UAP: Authenticate through EOSC AAI. Individual environments may be open, moderated or restricted; the relevant record must state the applicable membership rule. AUP: Infrastructure AUP, environment-specific rules, quotas and conditions attached to processed data and software. Explore environments Infrastructure AUP/UAP Training and collaboration Public + EOSC AAI Support education, skills development, file synchronisation and sharing, and collaboration across research communities. UAP: Open learning materials may be anonymous; personalised workspaces and collaboration functions require EOSC AAI and may have community-specific membership rules. AUP: Infrastructure or provider AUP, copyright and licensing conditions, storage quotas and collaboration rules. Find training and collaboration resources EOSC AAI sign-in How to read access status Public Available anonymously, although contribution functions may require authentication. Open EOSC AAI An EOSC user may authenticate and access under the stated limits. Moderated / allocation Access requires a request, approval or resource allocation. Restricted Access is limited to an identified community or project. The individual catalogue record is authoritative. It must name the provider, purpose, access route, AUP, UAP, licence and any quota or eligibility conditions. Scientific impact Federation in practice Cross-Node use cases demonstrate how federated resources can support reproducible workflows and secure distributed analysis. 1 Federating CERN REANA pipelines Execute containerised analyses where very large scientific datasets are held, reducing unnecessary movement of data and supporting reproducible near-data computation. 2 Multi-centric AI validation Contribute to a secure cross-Node environment for validating an AI model for prostate-cancer screening against data held by different hospitals. 3 Federated sensitive-data analysis Combine interactive notebooks, distributed HPC resources and certified cloud regions where the applicable authorisations and safeguards are in place. Read the official scientific-impact descriptions on eosc.eu → Node access and policies Clear conditions before access The landing page and public resource metadata are available without login. Authentication is required only when entering a protected environment or invoking a protected service. EOSC AAI access Select Sign in with EOSC AAI , choose an EOSC-compatible or academic identity offered by the access service, authenticate with the identity provider, and return to the requested resource. Open the EOSC-compliant login → Acceptable Use Policy D4Science-hosted services use the combined Access and Acceptable Use Policy. Federated providers may apply their own AUP, security rules and resource limits, linked from the resource record. Read the D4Science AUP → User Access Policy Each resource record must state whether access is public, open through EOSC AAI, moderated, allocated or restricted, and identify eligibility, approval, quotas and duration where applicable. Review resource access conditions → Resource conditions Datasets, archives, software and research products retain their licences, attribution requirements and provider conditions. A product licence may provide its AUP/UAP where appropriate. Read the research artefact policy → Privacy and data protection Personal-data processing is governed by the applicable Node, infrastructure and provider privacy statements. Sensitive-data services require additional safeguards and authorisation. Read the D4Science privacy policy → EOSC Federation context The dedicated eosc.eu entry records the Node’s scope, capabilities, access points, status, coordination and participating organisations. Open the official Node entry → Governance Coordinated and operated by ICSC ICSC — Italian Research Center on High Performance Computing, Big Data and Quantum Computing coordinates and operates EOSC Node | Italy with more than 50 Italian research-performing organisations, e-infrastructures and research infrastructures. The Node organisation includes CNR, INFN and GARR and represents more than 20 ERICs and ESFRIs. Its coordination and management team is documented on the dedicated EOSC Federation page. ICSC · Coordinating organisation CNR INFN GARR CINECA Italian RPOs National e-infrastructures 20+ ERICs and ESFRIs ICDI · National coordination support See the official coordination and contributors list → Node helpdesk and contact How can we help? For EOSC-AAI sign-in problems, Gateway incidents or questions about using the D4Science-hosted access point, open a request through the infrastructure support portal. Open the support portal For Node coordination, participation and policy questions, contact ICSC: info@supercomputing-icsc.it For a resource-specific scientific or access question, use the provider contact in the relevant catalogue record. EOSC Node | Italy is coordinated and operated by ICSC with Italian research organisations, e-infrastructures and research infrastructures. The Gateway is powered by D4Science and supported by ICDI. EOSC AAI sign-in Node Catalogue Official Node entry AUP/UAP Privacy Helpdesk

children.main_text: Terms of Use Defines the legal relationship between users and the D4Science infrastructure, including conditions of use, responsibilities, and limitations of liability. This is the final version 1.1 of the Terms of Use, which entered into force on 1 April 2026. Introduction These Terms of Use (“Terms”) define the conditions under which users may access and use the D4Science Infrastructure and the services provided through it. D4Science is a digital research infrastructure designed to support scientific communities by providing integrated environments where users can manage data, perform analyses, collaborate, and publish research results. These environments, known as Virtual Research Environments (VREs), enable distributed communities to work together using shared tools and resources. By accessing or using any component of the D4Science infrastructure, users acknowledge that they have read and understood these Terms and agree to comply with them. Users also acknowledge that the infrastructure operates within a broader governance framework composed of multiple policies, which collectively regulate its use. Purpose of the Infrastructure The D4Science infrastructure has been designed to support the full lifecycle of scientific research. It provides a set of integrated services that allow research communities to create, manage, analyse, and share knowledge in a collaborative digital environment. Through its Virtual Research Environments, D4Science enables: collaborative data analysis and interpretation management and sharing of research artefacts execution of computational workflows publication and discovery of research outputs The infrastructure promotes the principles of Open Science, encouraging transparency, reproducibility, and responsible sharing of scientific knowledge. Acknowledgement and Citation of D4Science D4Science is the result of sustained scientific and technological effort and is maintained as a shared research infrastructure. For this reason, users are strongly encouraged to acknowledge the use of the infrastructure in any scientific outputs produced with its support. Recommended citation [names removed__] (2019) Enacting Open Science by D4Science . Future Gener. Comput. Syst. 101: 555-563 https://doi.org/10.1016/j.future.2019.05.063 Additional guidance on how to cite D4Science, including references to specific services or Virtual Research Environments, is available at: https://www.d4science.org/how-cite Acknowledging the use of D4Science contributes to the visibility and sustainability of the infrastructure and supports its continued development. A suggested acknowledgement statement is: “This work has been enabled by the D4Science infrastructure ( https://www.d4science.org - ROR: https://ror.org/027cvs066 ).” Infrastructure Operator The D4Science infrastructure is operated by the Consiglio Nazionale delle Ricerche (CNR) through the Institute of Information Science and Technologies “A. Faedo” (ISTI) located in Pisa, Italy. The infrastructure is managed by a dedicated operational team, the D4Science Working Group, which is responsible for its design, operation, maintenance, and continuous evolution. The governance of the infrastructure includes an Executive Directorate that provides strategic direction and ensures alignment with scientific and institutional objectives. Definitions For clarity, the following terms are used throughout these Terms and the associated policy framework. D4Science Infrastructure: A distributed digital research infrastructure providing services, computing resources, and collaborative environments to scientific communities. Gateway: A web-based access point through which users authenticate and access infrastructure services. Virtual Research Environment (VRE): A customizable collaborative environment created for a specific research community or project. A VRE acts as a logical security context in which access to services and resources is controlled. Service: Any capability provided by the infrastructure, including data management, computational, collaboration, and API-based services. Research Artefact: Any digital resource used or produced within the infrastructure to support research activities, including datasets, models, workflows, software, scripts, notebooks, and applications. Scope of the Infrastructure The D4Science infrastructure provides a wide range of services supporting research activities, including data management, collaborative tools, computational platforms, and programmatic access through APIs. The infrastructure operates on a distributed model and may integrate resources hosted across: infrastructure managed by CNR infrastructure provided by GARR approved cloud providers As part of its evolution, the infrastructure periodically updates its services. For example, the DataMiner platform has been replaced by the Cloud Computing Platform (CCP), with legacy support planned until October 2026. Relationship with Other Policies These Terms are part of the D4Science Policy Framework, which includes several complementary documents addressing different aspects of infrastructure governance. These include: Access and Acceptable Use Policy Privacy and Data Protection Policy Service Policy Security and Incident Response Policy Data and Research Artefact Governance and Licensing Policy By accepting these Terms, users acknowledge that these policies apply to their use of the infrastructure. Eligibility for Access Access to the D4Science infrastructure is intended for individuals and organizations engaged in research, education, or related activities. Users typically access the infrastructure through a Gateway and may join one or more Virtual Research Environments, depending on their role and the policies defined by each community. Each VRE may define its own access rules and participation criteria. User Responsibilities Users play a key role in ensuring the proper use of the infrastructure. They are expected to use the services responsibly and in compliance with applicable laws and regulations. In particular, users must: ensure that they have the right to use and share any research artefacts they upload respect intellectual property and licensing conditions avoid actions that could compromise the security or stability of the infrastructure Responsibility: Users are responsible for maintaining the confidentiality of their credentials and for all activities performed through their accounts. Intellectual Property Users retain ownership of the research artefacts they upload, create, or manage within the infrastructure. By using the infrastructure, users grant the operator a non-exclusive licence to process such artefacts solely for the purpose of providing the services. The infrastructure operator does not claim ownership of user-generated content. Security and Monitoring The D4Science infrastructure implements security measures designed to protect its systems and users. These measures include authentication controls, monitoring of system activity, and logging of relevant events. Monitoring activities are carried out in accordance with applicable laws and institutional policies. The security framework of the infrastructure is aligned with recognized best practices and with the principles introduced by the NIS2 Directive. Service Availability The infrastructure operator makes reasonable efforts to ensure that services are available and reliable. However, services are provided on a best-effort basis, and availability may vary depending on operational conditions. Typical availability targets exceed 99.5%, although temporary interruptions may occur due to maintenance or unforeseen issues. Changes to Services D4Science evolves continuously to meet the needs of research communities and to adapt to technological and regulatory changes. Services may be updated, replaced, or discontinued over time. When possible, users will be informed in advance of significant changes affecting the services they use. Limitation of Liability The infrastructure is provided without guarantees regarding uninterrupted availability or the accuracy of results produced through its use. The operator is not responsible for: loss of data, service interruptions, inaccuracies in research artefacts, or results generated through computational services. Users remain responsible for validating their results. Termination of Access and Governing Law Access to the infrastructure may be suspended or terminated in cases such as: violation of applicable policies, security risks, misuse of services, or prolonged inactivity. Such measures are taken to protect the integrity of the infrastructure and its users. These Terms are governed by the laws of Italy. Policy Framework This document forms part of the D4Science Policy Framework .
